countercurrent.title: Gill lamella: flip the blood
countercurrent.concurrentNote: Same direction: water and blood rush to a shared, middling balance and stop — the slope dies at the halfway mark and the leftover oxygen drifts past untaken.
countercurrent.countercurrentNote: Opposed: the blood always meets water fresher than itself, so the slope holds the whole length of the frond — oxygen is taken right to the end.

breathingMode.title: Two ways to breathe, one problem
breathingMode.tidalNote: Tidal: air in and back out the same door, leaving a pocket of stale air that never clears; every breath stops and reverses a heavy mass of gas. In Pandora's dense air, that cost is steep.
breathingMode.unidirectionalNote: One-way: air streams a single direction across an always-fresh surface, never pausing, never reversing. Forward-facing intakes let the animal's own speed do the pumping — almost free.

steps.label: Luciferin + O₂
steps.body: The enzyme luciferase takes a small fuel molecule — luciferin — and joins it to oxygen. No light yet; this is only loading the chamber.

steps.label: High-energy intermediate
steps.body: Oxidation builds a strained peroxide ring (a dioxetanone). When the ring snaps, it sheds CO₂ and kicks the product up into an excited electronic state.

steps.label: Photon
steps.body: The excited electron drops back to its ground state. The whole energy difference leaves as a single particle of light — with almost no waste heat. That is cold light.

photophore.title: Photophore
photophore.info: A built lamp: photocyte, reflector, lens, pigment shutter. Toggle each layer and watch the beam shape change.

glowBiogeography.title: Where glow happens — and why
glowBiogeography.insight: One rule, flipped: bioluminescence floods wherever it is chronically dim and a visual signal pays. On Earth that is the deep sea; dim Polyphemus-lit nights turn Pandora's land into the deep sea too.

glowOriginsTree.title: One trick, invented dozens of times
glowOriginsTree.hint: Tap a branch to see its own fuel and enzyme.
glowOriginsTree.note: Each branch glows with a different fuel molecule and a different enzyme. They did not inherit light from a shared glowing ancestor — every lineage stumbled onto it on its own.

umweltLens.title: One scene, four worlds
umweltLens.subtitle: The same patch of night forest, re-seen through different senses
umweltLens.umgebung: The shared world — one forest, unchanged

hint.human: A human's visible-light world: near-black, a few failing instrument glows, almost everything filtered out before it arrives.
hint.navi: Na'vi night vision lifts the whole scene — a large, tapetum-backed eye squeezing every photon, the forest legible in the dark.
hint.magnetic: The magnetoreceptive channel: field lines that pass straight through a human unfelt are drawn as a navigable map.
hint.biolum: The reactive-light channel: a footstep blooms into a cascade and the flora signals — a whole conversation a human barely sees.

predatorPrey.title: The coupled wheel
predatorPrey.subtitle: Same hunt, three models — watch how each answers a shock

note.naive: The naive Lotka-Volterra wheel: a neutrally stable orbit. Nudge it and it drifts to a new orbit and stays there — nothing pulls it back. A balance any breath of wind can move.
note.real: Add a carrying capacity and a saturating hunter and the orbit gains a true resting point: nudge it and it spirals back. This is the density-dependent forest that survives shocks.
note.enriched: Raise the carrying capacity far — enrich the world — and the orbit swings wider and wider, its troughs grazing zero. The paradox of enrichment: more food makes the system more likely to crash.

predatorPrey.ariaTime: Time-series of hexapede and viperwolf populations rising and falling out of step
predatorPrey.ariaPhase: Phase-plane orbit of hexapede against viperwolf numbers

functionalResponse.title: How fast one hunter eats
functionalResponse.subtitle: Drag the prey density — watch the share each hunter takes

type1.role: A filter-feeder straining food from the water — intake just tracks how thick the prey is, until it is full.
type1.note: Type I: a straight line to a hard cap. Search and swallow are one act, so the kill rate climbs in direct proportion to prey, then stops dead at satiety. The shape of a filter-feeder.

type2.role: A solitary hunter limited by handling time — it can only stalk, kill, and eat so fast no matter how thick the herds grow.
type2.note: Type II: climbs steeply, then bends to a ceiling set by handling time. At low prey density the hunter takes a larger fraction of what little remains — quietly destabilising, pressing rare prey rarer.

type3.role: A learning, switching hunter that ignores rare prey until there is enough to be worth forming a search image for.
type3.note: Type III: the S-curve, nearly flat near the origin before it rises and levels off. That flat stretch is a refuge — when prey get rare, the pressure eases instead of tightening, letting a crashing population recover. The strongest behavioural stabiliser there is.

forestDive.title: Vertical Forest Dive
forestDive.subtitle: Drag the elevator to sink through the layers and watch the climate change
forestDive.hint: Drag the slider to dive from the canopy to the forest floor. Watch how light decays exponentially when blocked by the canopy, humidity rises, wind dies down, and temperature swings are buffered.

fauna.0: Banshees roost on the peaks, catching wind and blistering sun.
fauna.1: Prolemuris swing through the dense canopy.
fauna.2: Na'vi hunt in the cool, shaded understory.
fauna.3: Hexapedes graze in the dim, still light of the forest floor.

keystoneCascade.title: Pull the keystone
keystoneCascade.subtitle: Draw out the apex wedge and watch the arch hold, then let go

phase.stable: The apex predator is the keystone wedge at the crown — the whole arch leans on one rare animal. Grazers are held in check and the vegetation stays lush.
phase.tipping: The wedge is most of the way out. The arch is losing its hold; the grazers are already climbing as the check on them weakens.
phase.collapsed: The keystone is gone and the arch lets go all at once — grazers explode, vegetation crashes, the smaller herbivores are crushed out. A collapse running top to bottom from removing a single rare animal.

xenobiologyLadder.aria: Pandora's biological claims plotted on a spectrum from all-but-forced to physically forbidden

nightEyeOptics.title: The night eye: a bucket for light
nightEyeOptics.subtitle: Widen the pupil to drink more photons — and pay on the way out
nightEyeOptics.aria: A nocturnal eye gathering more light as its pupil widens, with the three optical costs rising in step
nightEyeOptics.hint: A wider pupil is a wider bucket held up to a thin rain of photons — but physics charges for it: graininess falls while edge blur rises and the in-focus slice grows shallow. The tapetum is a mirror behind the retina that bounces missed photons back for a second pass, the same trick that flares a cat's eyes in headlights.

magneticCompass.title: Two machines for one missing sense
magneticCompass.subtitle: A quantum compass reads direction; a magnetite map reads where you are
magneticCompass.mapWhy: rugged crystals hold where the quantum compass fails
magneticCompass.calmNote: In a quiet, steady field both machines work: the quantum compass in the eye paints the field's angle across vision (direction), while magnetite crystals read raw intensity (position). Earth's birds run both.
magneticCompass.vortexNote: Drop into the flux vortex and the delicate quantum compass scrambles — its coherence shattered by the noisy field, the overlay breaking into static. The rugged magnetite map holds. A flyer that thrives here must lean on the tough machine, which is why banshees fly the vortex clean where human instruments go blind.

chirality.title: Chirality & Optical Rotation
chirality.hint: Rotate the analyzer dial to align with the rotated light plane. Chiral molecules rotate polarized light clockwise (D-form) or counterclockwise (L-form).

carbonSilicon.title: The breath that decides it
carbonSilicon.subtitle: Burn each element and look at the exhaust — one leaves, one stays
carbonSilicon.solid: a solid — quartz, no way out
carbonSilicon.carbonNote: Burn carbon for energy and the exhaust is CO₂ — a gas. It dissolves in blood, rides to the lungs, and leaves on the next breath. Waste disposal is built into the chemistry, and carbon's bonds are strong enough to last yet weak enough to rearrange.
carbonSilicon.siliconNote: Burn silicon and the exhaust is SiO₂ — quartz, sand, a solid. With every breath the airway fills with rock it cannot exhale, until the metabolism bricks itself shut. Silicon's weaker bonds also fall apart past a few atoms in a row. Silicon does not metabolize; it petrifies.

quorumCascade.title: A network that decides with no decider
quorumCascade.subtitle: Inject a distress signal at the most connected node and watch local thresholds do all the work
quorumCascade.aria: A grid of agents wired to their neighbours; a distress signal injected at the central node spreads outward when enough neighbours are roused
quorumCascade.scrubLabel: Scrub through the cascade tick by tick
quorumCascade.quorumLow: Tips on a single roused neighbour — spreads like wildfire
quorumCascade.quorumMid: Two roused neighbours flip a quiet agent
quorumCascade.quorumHigh: Hard to tip — the alarm struggles to travel
quorumCascade.noDecider: No node chose this — thresholds did
quorumCascade.prompt: Inject a distress signal at the Tree of Souls node. With a low quorum the alarm sweeps the whole network; raise it and the same signal dies out locally. Either way, nothing decides — the threshold does.
quorumCascade.cascadeNote: The signal crossed the quorum at enough nodes to ignite the whole network — exactly how Pandora's wildlife could mobilize without a goddess issuing a command. A reflex, not a choice.
quorumCascade.containedNote: The quorum was too high for the signal to travel, so the alarm stayed local — an immune flare that fizzled. The network 'chose' nothing; the threshold simply wasn't met.

integrationVsSize.title: Bigger is not a mind
integrationVsSize.subtitle: Raw connection count does not make consciousness — architecture does
integrationVsSize.aria: Two networks compared: a vast one-way feed-forward mesh with near-zero integration, and a small densely recurrent loop with high integration
integrationVsSize.oneWay: signal flows one way, never back
integrationVsSize.meshNote: A colossal one-way mesh — signal enters, passes through, exits, and never loops back. This is the cerebellum: 69 billion neurons, 80% of the brain, and almost nothing to do with consciousness. Eywa's planet of slow root-links is built the same way.
integrationVsSize.loopNote: A far smaller web, but every node talks back to the others — information reverberates, integrates, binds. This is the cortex, and under IIT it is recurrent feedback, not sheer size, that earns a non-zero Φ. The map matters more than the headcount.

claimAudit.title: Auditing the claim
claimAudit.subtitle: Three claims, three very different burdens of proof

hint.well-supported: Solid ground: the basic biology of a shared fungal web is not in doubt.
hint.demonstrated-under-conditions: Footing thins: transfer happens, but the amount and the path are hard to pin down.
hint.contested: Open air: the most beloved claim has zero field evidence behind it.

mycorrhizalMarket.title: The underground market
mycorrhizalMarket.subtitle: You are the plant. Pay carbon, see what phosphorus comes back.
mycorrhizalMarket.aria: An interactive trade between a plant and a fungus, sending carbon and receiving phosphorus

verdict.reward: A fair partner, well paid, pays you back — so you route it more carbon. Reciprocal reward.
verdict.sanction: You are underpaying a willing partner and getting little back. Pay more, or it favours a better customer.
verdict.cheated: This partner hoards phosphorus no matter how much you pay. The plant learns to starve it — a sanction.

percolationNetwork.title: Burn it down — and find the cliff
percolationNetwork.subtitle: Remove part of a scale-free network and watch what stays connected
percolationNetwork.aria: A scale-free network of glowing nodes and links; removing nodes either at random or hubs-first, showing the largest surviving connected component
percolationNetwork.giantNote: share of the whole still wired into one piece
percolationNetwork.hubHint: big nodes = hubs · small nodes = leaves
percolationNetwork.randomHint: Removing nodes blindly, by where they sit — not by how connected they are
percolationNetwork.targetedHint: Removing the most-connected hubs first — the Albert-Barabási attack
percolationNetwork.prompt: Drag to remove part of the network. Under random removal the giant component clings on far past where you would expect, then vanishes all at once at the percolation threshold. Switch to targeted and aim at the hubs — the same network shatters after only a few.
percolationNetwork.randomNote: Random loss barely dents the connected whole — the leaves fall, the hubs hold, and signals route around the damage. This is why clear-cutting forests never kills the network.
percolationNetwork.targetedNote: Striking the hubs first tears the network apart fast. Only a small fraction of removals — the right fraction — drops the giant component off a cliff. This is Quaritch's instinct at the Tree of Souls.
percolationNetwork.shatteredNote: The giant component is gone: what remains is a dust of disconnected islands that cannot reach each other. Below the percolation threshold the network is no longer one whole — it is fragments.

cascadingFailure.title: The cascade — kill her without a fire
cascadingFailure.subtitle: Two coupled networks, and a plague that touches only one
cascadingFailure.aria: Two facing rows of nodes — flora above, fauna below — each depending on a partner in the other; {dead} of {total} nodes have failed
cascadingFailure.roundNote: each round, failure crosses to the other layer
cascadingFailure.prompt: Release a plague that kills only animals — not a single tree. Then step the cascade and watch the damage ricochet: dead fauna strand the flora that depended on them, dead flora starve the fauna that depended on those, an avalanche bouncing between two layers each of which was robust on its own.
cascadingFailure.stepHint: Keep stepping. The failure has not settled — it is still bouncing between the two layers, each round taking down whatever lost its partner in the last.
cascadingFailure.settledNote: The cascade has settled. A plague aimed at one layer alone has pulled both down together — the signature of interdependent networks (Buldyrev et al. 2010).
cascadingFailure.collapsedNote: Both networks are gone. The most efficient way to kill a forest, the mathematics suggests, may be to never touch the forest at all — only the creatures it cannot live without.

forestStrata.title: One forest, four stacked worlds
forestStrata.lightNote: share of canopy-top sunlight that survives
forestStrata.prompt: Click a layer to see its light budget, climate, and the Pandoran life that lives at that height.
forestStrata.hint: A forest is not one habitat but a stack of them, sorted by height. The amber curve is the surviving light, falling off exponentially through the leaves (Beer-Lambert) — by the floor of a closed forest as little as 1–2% of the canopy-top sun is left. Each floor is a different world, and the animals sort themselves accordingly.

strataDiversity.title: Biodiversity Multiplier
strataDiversity.subtitle: Grow the tree taller to see how vertical strata multiply niches
strataDiversity.hint: Use the slider to grow the tree. As new layers emerge, new ecological niches open up without competing for space.

lotkaVolterra.title: Predator-Prey Population dynamics
lotkaVolterra.hint: Adjust birth, predation, and death rates. Enable Prey-switching to stabilize oscillations, or introduce a Carrying Capacity (K) to test the Paradox of Enrichment.

umwelt.title: Umwelt
umwelt.info: Each creature's sensory bubble. Flip among five bodies; spectra and senses overlap or diverge — worlds inside one forest.

aposematism.title: Aposematism
aposematism.info: Honest warning colors. Bright signals advertise real cost — toxin, spine, sting. Toggle a predator approach; dim the signal until the retreat threshold fails.

bioluminescence.title: Bioluminescence
bioluminescence.info: Cold light from life. Step luciferin → luciferase → excited state → photon. Advance each stage; the glow climbs without waste heat.

chemiluminescence.title: Chemiluminescence
chemiluminescence.info: Same electronic jump, no enzyme. Side-by-side with bioluminescence: both emit, but the living path runs cooler.

counter-illumination.title: Counter-Illumination
counter-illumination.info: Ventral glow cancels a silhouette from below. Toggle photophores; the dark body dissolves into the downwelling light.

cryptochrome.title: Cryptochrome
cryptochrome.info: A radical-pair compass in the eye. Rotate the field; singlet/triplet balance tips and the internal needle shifts.

dead-space.title: Dead Space
dead-space.info: Air that moves but never exchanges. Deepen the breath; dead-space fraction falls as tidal volume climbs past the conduit.

echolocation.title: Echolocation
echolocation.info: Pulse out, echo home. Move the target; round-trip time becomes range. Hearing as a ruler.

electroreception.title: Electroreception
electroreception.info: Living voltmeters in water. Move the prey; field lines warp and snout receptors light where the distortion peaks.

ficks-law.title: Fick's Law
ficks-law.info: Flux ∝ area × ΔC / thickness. Thin the membrane, steepen the gradient; O₂ rate climbs. Pandoran fans win on both levers.

fluorescence.title: Fluorescence
fluorescence.info: Absorb short, emit long — the Stokes shift. Pick a fluorophore; watch emission color slide redward of the excitation.

gill-lamella.title: Gill Lamella
gill-lamella.info: Stacked plates, countercurrent blood. Flip to parallel flow and extraction efficiency halves — geometry is the engine.

green-fluorescent-protein.title: Green Fluorescent Protein
green-fluorescent-protein.info: A β-barrel lamp. Blue in, green out; the chromophore at the core pulses. Sweep excitation and the glow answers.

histotoxic-hypoxia.title: Histotoxic Hypoxia
histotoxic-hypoxia.info: O₂ arrives; cells cannot use it. Blocked mitochondria sit dark while oxygen piles up unused — cyanide's quiet asphyxia.

hypercapnia.title: Hypercapnia
hypercapnia.info: CO₂ climbs; respiratory drive screams. Raise pCO₂ and the urge-to-breathe signal spikes — Na'vi physiology must blunt this.

lateral-line.title: Lateral Line
lateral-line.info: A touch sense for water. Wave near the canal; hair cells deflect and fire along the flank.

luciferin.title: Luciferin
luciferin.info: The fuel molecule of cold light. Highlight the reactive site where oxygen docks before the photon is born.

luciferase.title: Luciferase
luciferase.info: The enzyme that lights the fuel. Dock luciferin, watch the pocket close, release oxyluciferin and a photon.

magnetite.title: Magnetite
magnetite.info: Fe₃O₄ crystals that torque a cell. Rotate the field; the chain turns the body like a living compass needle.

magnetoreception.title: Magnetoreception
magnetoreception.info: Two compasses in one bird: cryptochrome in the eye, magnetite in the beak. Toggle each; navigation accuracy shifts.

magnetosome.title: Magnetosome
magnetosome.info: A chain of magnetite organelles. Apply a field; the chain and cell rotate together. Remove it — the chain keeps its memory.

nerve-conduction-velocity.title: Nerve Conduction Velocity
nerve-conduction-velocity.info: Myelin turns a crawl into a leap. Compare continuous vs saltatory spikes; the speed readout jumps with sheath.

operculum.title: Operculum
operculum.info: The gill cover as a pump. Open–close pushes water across lamellae. Switch to ram ventilation — mouth open, cover locked, swim for breath.

proprioception.title: Proprioception
proprioception.info: The sense of self-position. Drag the limb; spindles fire on stretch, Golgi organs on load — the body reading itself.

quantum-yield.title: Quantum Yield
quantum-yield.info: Photons out per reaction in. Tune pH, temperature, O₂; the yield meter shows how often chemistry becomes light.

radical-pair.title: Radical Pair
radical-pair.info: Two unpaired spins as a molecular compass. A weak field tips singlet vs triplet; the product ratio is the signal cryptochrome reads.

ram-ventilation.title: Ram Ventilation
ram-ventilation.info: Swim to breathe. Below threshold speed the fish must pump; above it, open mouth and locked operculum do the work.

spiracle.title: Spiracle
spiracle.info: Side doors on an insect thorax. Open them; O₂ diffuses in along tracheae. Close them; exchange stalls.

tapetum-lucidum.title: Tapetum Lucidum
tapetum-lucidum.info: A night mirror behind the retina. Dim the world; light double-passes and eyeshine blooms.

tidal-ventilation.title: Tidal Ventilation
tidal-ventilation.info: In and out the same path. Mark tidal, residual, capacity; dead space rides along — compare to unidirectional fans.

unidirectional-airflow.title: Unidirectional Airflow
unidirectional-airflow.info: Air crosses exchange tissue one way only. Efficiency bar beats mammalian tidal back-and-forth — bird and Pandoran strategy.

cross-current-exchange.title: Cross-Current Exchange
cross-current-exchange.info: Three geometries: concurrent, countercurrent, cross-current. Efficiency bars rank them — fans may sit in the cross-current middle.

countercurrent-exchange.title: Countercurrent Exchange
countercurrent-exchange.info: Two flows, opposite directions. Gradients stay steep the whole length — maximum transfer versus same-way concurrent waste.

soilPoreExplorer.title: A pore is a continent
soilPoreExplorer.subtitle: Water connects microbial neighbours, then shuts the oxygen door

aria.dry: A dry soil pore with broken water films and isolated microorganisms
aria.moist: A moist soil pore with connected water films, oxygen, and active microorganisms
aria.saturated: A flooded soil pore with thick water, weak oxygen diffusion, and anoxic pockets

verdict.dry: Air is plentiful, but the water highways are broken. Cells cannot reach substrate or one another.
verdict.moist: Thin connected films deliver substrate while gas-filled space still supplies oxygen—the busy middle.
verdict.saturated: Water reconnects the pore but oxygen diffuses slowly through it. Different anaerobic metabolisms take over.

hint.dry: Drying does not empty a pore; it divides it into microbial islands.
hint.moist: Maximum biological activity usually sits between drought and flooding, where water and oxygen coexist.
hint.saturated: A flooded pore is not dead. It changes chemistry: denitrification, fermentation, and methanogenesis become possible.

redQueenRace.title: The target that will not stay still
redQueenRace.subtitle: Compare directional escalation with a Red Queen cycle
redQueenRace.tracking: the pathogen tracks what is common
redQueenRace.armsAria: Directional escalation between defence and attack
redQueenRace.armsExplanation: The same trait ratchets upward on both sides. Older variants are replaced rather than returning when rare.
redQueenRace.armsVerdict: Each improvement selects for a stronger countermeasure.

hint.fluctuating: The common host becomes the easiest target. Rarity is temporarily valuable, so genotypes cycle instead of marching toward one permanent winner.
hint.armsRace: An arms race is directional: defence and attack accumulate. Red Queen dynamics can instead preserve old variants by making rarity itself advantageous.

soil-aggregate.title: A soil world built from crumbs
soil-aggregate.info: Roots, fungal threads, and microbial glues bind mineral grains into porous aggregates.
soil-aggregate.caption: Millimetres of distance can separate contrasting habitats.

decomposition.title: Matter changes hands
decomposition.info: Decomposition transfers dead material through fragmenters, microbes, and living tissue.
decomposition.caption: Nothing vanishes; carbon and nutrients change form and owner.

rhizosphere.title: The root's moving halo
rhizosphere.info: Root exudates make the narrow soil zone around a growing tip chemically distinct.
rhizosphere.caption: A plant spends carbon to shape the microbial neighbourhood around it.

microbiome.title: A community, not an organ
microbiome.info: A microbiome includes microorganisms, their genes, and their activity in one habitat.
microbiome.caption: Helpful, neutral, and harmful members can occupy the same community.

pathogen.title: Disease is a sequence of gates
pathogen.info: A would-be pathogen must reach, enter, reproduce in, and leave a compatible host.
pathogen.caption: Failure at any gate ends the infection chain.

negative-frequency-dependent-selection.title: Rarity has temporary value
negative-frequency-dependent-selection.info: A variant loses advantage as it becomes common and easier for enemies to track.
negative-frequency-dependent-selection.caption: Today's escape type becomes tomorrow's familiar target.

red-queen-hypothesis.title: Running to stay in place
red-queen-hypothesis.info: Hosts and parasites continually alter one another's selective environment.
red-queen-hypothesis.caption: Relative fitness can stay level while both sides keep evolving.

planetary-protection.title: Keep two biospheres apart
planetary-protection.info: Planetary protection limits forward contamination and safeguards returned samples.
planetary-protection.caption: Containment protects ecosystems and the meaning of the scientific result.

foundationVsKeystone.title: Two kinds of important
foundationVsKeystone.subtitle: Plot an organism by its bulk and by what its removal costs
foundationVsKeystone.hint: Robert Paine's keystone was rare and worked by eating; a foundation species is most of the biomass and works by physically existing. Divide impact by abundance and the two separate cleanly. Hometree sits in the far foundation corner — which is why calling it a keystone is a category error rather than a compliment.

verdict.keystone: Punches far above its weight — the disproportion is the definition.
verdict.foundation: Impact matches its mass. Nothing disproportionate: it is the habitat.
verdict.dominant: Monopolises resources, but little depends on its structure.
verdict.passenger: Present, and the community barely registers its loss.

structureClock.title: The two clocks of recovery
structureClock.subtitle: Scrub across four orders of magnitude and watch the curves refuse to travel together
structureClock.hint: Green cover returns fast: pioneers within a season, full standing biomass in 30-80 years. Structure does not. Small hollows begin at about 110 years, large cavities need 220-500, and full old-growth complexity runs to centuries or millennia. The gap between the curves is everything a replanted forest does not yet have.
structureClock.timeLabel: Years since the forest was cleared

verdict.noStructure: Green, and structurally empty. No hollow exists yet at any age below about a century.
verdict.lookingRecovered: Looks recovered from the air. To anything that needs a cavity or canopy soil, it is a construction site.
verdict.genuinelyOld: Structure has finally caught up. This is what old growth means, and what cannot be planted.

milestone.pioneers: ~3 yr — pioneer vegetation covers the ash
milestone.canopyClosed: ~60 yr — canopy closed, biomass nearly full
milestone.firstHollows: ~110 yr — the first small hollows begin to form
milestone.largeCavities: ~350 yr — cavities big enough for large vertebrates
milestone.oldGrowth: ~800 yr — deep bark, canopy soil, full complexity
